newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia-Pacific women seek united voice in APEC.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific women seek united voice in APEC.

text.p: Senior women community and business leaders called on Friday for their new network to be recognised as a "strategic partner" within the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

More than 60 women from 14 of the 18 APEC member economies ended a three-day conference in Manila saying they were determined that women's interests should not be overlooked as the region moves towards trade liberalisation.
The meeting formalised the setting up of the APEC Senior Women Leader's Network.
"Our first success is just to form a group," Malee Suwana-Adth, a consultant at Thailand's National Science and Technology Development Agency, told a news conference.
"By having women as part of the APEC process, we hope to fill in the missing parts of the APEC process (to help it) to become a 21st Century family institution," she said.
Conference participants said that few women had participated in APEC ministerial meetings, paving the way for the region to abolish all trade barriers by the year 2020.
As a result, they said, they feared that women's interests and needs may not be fully represented.
Imelda Nicolas, the Network's Filipina chairperson, said representatives of the group would meet Philippine President Fidel Ramos to ask him to endorse women's participation in APEC.
The Philippines will host this year's APEC leaders' summit in November.
Network organisers say there is growing concern that free trade could alter regional employment patterns and that women were often in the front line when jobs had to be cut.
They say there is also a need for bilateral and multilateral agreements to protect female migrant workers.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore and the United States.
